guitar.guitaristsText: Josh Homme (lead guitar, bass, vocals, electric piano) / Troy Van Leeuwen (rhythm guitar, lap steel)
guitar.modelsText: Maton BB1200 (Homme) / Fender Jaguar & Fender Jazzmaster (Van Leeuwen)
models: Fender Jaguar (1963, refinished black, orig. Candy Apple Red)
guitar.evidence: Wikipedia's personnel credits for '3's & 7's' confirm Homme on lead guitar/bass/electric piano and Van Leeuwen on rhythm guitar/lap steel. Guitar.com/Guitar World interviews with Van Leeuwen document his switch to offset single-coils (a black-refinished '63 Jaguar and a '62 Jazzmaster reissue) starting on Era Vulgaris, moving away from humbucker-dominated tones. Guitar Lobby/Mixdown corroborate the Maton BB1200 was acquired right as Era Vulgaris tracking began.
guitar.notes: Corrected the original sheet: the 'Ovation Ultra GP' is a guitar tied to earlier/other eras of Homme's career and is not specifically documented for this song, so it was dropped in favor of era-appropriate, sourced instruments. The song is widely tabbed in QOTSA's frequent two-whole-step-down tuning (C F Bb Eb G C), consistent with much of the Lullabies to Paralyze/Era Vulgaris material, but this specific detail comes from crowd-sourced tab sites (Ultimate-Guitar), not a direct artist statement — treat tuning as medium confidence only.
guitar.source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3's_&_7's (personnel); guitar.com and guitarworld.com interviews with Troy Van Leeuwen; guitarlobby.com and mixdownmag.com.au Josh Homme gear profiles; tabs.ultimate-guitar.com (tuning, secondary)

tone.target: dry, mid-forward garage/desert-rock grind with vintage octave-fuzz bite; tight and driving rather than sludgy or wall-of-gain
tone.profile: dry, mid-forward garage/desert-rock grind with vintage octave-fuzz bite
tone.summary: A tight, riff-driven tone built on a push-mids American amp voicing (Homme's signature Ampeg-style sound) rather than a British stack, with a vintage-flavored fuzz for bite and offset single-coil guitars (Jaguar/Jazzmaster) adding snap over the older humbucker-based QOTSA sound.
mustHave: dry, close-mic feel with minimal reverb
upper/low-mid EQ push (~400-600 Hz boost documented across QOTSA sessions)
avoid: boomy low end from oversized cabs
gearClues: Ampeg VT-40-style mid-push amp (Homme's most consistently documented amp; not a Marshall/Plexi)
vintage-style fuzz with octave character (Univox Super-Fuzz / Fulltone Ultimate Octave associated with this era)
offset single-coil guitars (Fender Jaguar/Jazzmaster) rather than humbucker solid-bodies
4x10-style cab rather than a 4x12 stack, per documented VT-40 live/studio setup
corrections: Replaced the unverified 'Marshall/Plexi-style amp' assumption with an Ampeg VT-40-style mid-push voicing, which is the amp actually and repeatedly documented for Homme's tone; flagged as a gap since GP-180 has no Ampeg model.
Replaced the generic '4x12 cab' clue with a 4x10-style cab clue, matching the VT-40's documented stage/studio cabinet configuration.

Replaced the vague 'fuzz or near-fuzz drive' with a vintage octave-fuzz character, based on forum/gear-analysis discussion specifically referencing this track (medium/low confidence — not a direct artist quote about this song).
Kept the drop of chorus/tremolo/big delay/lush reverb — consistent with QOTSA's generally dry studio approach documented across multiple production write-ups.

rig.name: Queens Of The Stone Age - 3's and 7's - Valeton GP-180
rig.recommendedGuitar: Offset single-coil guitar (Fender Jaguar/Jazzmaster-style) in bridge or bridge+middle position for authenticity; a Maton BB1200-style semi-hollow is Homme's own alternate. A Telecaster/Stratocaster bridge pickup is a practical substitute if an offset isn't available.

blocks.purpose: Clean up hum/noise inherent to a pushed-mids fuzz tone.
blocks.gap: None — standard utility gate, no song-specific evidence needed.

blocks.purpose: Approximates a clean boost (Homme's rig has documented boosts like a Fulltone Fat-Boost / Zvex Super Hard On) pushing the amp front end for extra punch and sustain.
blocks.gap: Clean-boost pedals are documented across Homme's live/studio rig generally, but not confirmed specifically for this track — treat as an educated inference.

alternatives.reason: A light compressor could substitute for sustain/attack control if boost feels too aggressive.

blocks.purpose: Included to fill the required WAH slot; no evidence supports wah/filter use on this specific track, so kept off.
blocks.gap: No source ties a wah/filter pedal to this song specifically; QOTSA does use static filters (e.g., a Maestro/Stone Deaf-style parametric filter) on other tracks, but not confirmed here.

blocks.purpose: Delivers the tight, vintage-flavored fuzz with an octave-ish edge associated with this track and era (Univox Super-Fuzz / Fulltone Ultimate Octave character).
blocks.gap: GP-180 has no dedicated octave-fuzz voicing; standard Fuzz used as the closest available character. The octave element is sourced from secondary forum/gear discussion (TheGearPage), not a direct artist interview about this song — treat as medium/low confidence.

alternatives.reason: Tighter, more modern-voiced drive if the vintage fuzz feels too loose/gated.
Thicker, more sustained fuzz matching QOTSA's general 'Big Muff-esque' textures used elsewhere in the catalog.

blocks.purpose: Approximates the mid-forward, Baxandall-EQ-pushed breakup that defines Homme's signature Ampeg VT-40 tone — Bassman-style circuits share that midrange push and are the closest available voicing.
blocks.gap: The real amp is an Ampeg VT-40 (Homme's most consistently documented amp across his career) — GP-180 has no Ampeg model. Bellman 59N (Fender Bassman-style) is used as the closest mid-forward analog. Van Leeuwen's guitars on Era Vulgaris were reportedly run through 'small, cheap amps,' a detail too vague to model precisely.

alternatives.reason: More generic Marshall Plexi-style desert-rock alternative if a fuller/British-voiced grind is preferred, though this is less historically accurate to the actual documented gear for this track.

blocks.purpose: Matches the 4x10 speaker configuration documented for Homme's Ampeg VT-40 rig ('VT-40s with a 4x10 cabinet can be seen on stage'), avoiding the boomier/broader spread of a 4x12.
blocks.gap: No true Ampeg cab model exists in this catalog; Bellman 4x10 is chosen for matching the correct speaker count/format rather than exact Ampeg voicing.

alternatives.reason: Slightly tighter, more modern alternative if 4x10 sounds too boxy for the mix.

blocks.purpose: Sculpts the 400-600 Hz push that multiple QOTSA production breakdowns describe as central to Homme's sound ('a huge part of Josh's sound is EQ, boosts to the mids and low-mids').
blocks.gap: The EQ approach (mid push) is well documented for QOTSA generally; the exact dB/Hz values here are a reasonable estimate, not measured from this specific recording.

blocks.purpose: Included to fill the required MOD slot; kept inactive to preserve the dry, unmodulated character the tone brief calls for.
blocks.gap: No modulation is documented or audible as central to this track; module present only for chain completeness.

blocks.purpose: Included to fill the required DLY slot; kept off to avoid the 'big delay' the tone brief explicitly avoids.
blocks.gap: No delay use is documented for this specific track.

blocks.purpose: Minimal ambience only, consistent with QOTSA's generally dry mixing approach documented across multiple production write-ups.
blocks.gap: None — low-mix room verb is a safe, well-supported choice for this dry aesthetic.

alternatives.reason: Slight alternative if a touch more sheen is wanted without adding audible wash.

improvements.summary: Priority fixes address the biggest gaps between documented gear and the GP-180 catalog: the missing Ampeg voicing and the missing octave-fuzz character.

proposals.recommendedAsset: User-loaded Ampeg VT-40 + 4x10 IR (e.g., a captured or third-party Ampeg IR)
proposals.reason: GP-180 has no native Ampeg model; a user IR would close the largest documented gap between this rig and Homme's actual signature tone.
proposals.whenToUse: As soon as a suitable IR is available; test against the Bellman 59N + Bellman 4x10 approximation.
proposals.expectedGain: Significantly closer amp/cab character to the real recorded tone.

proposals.recommendedAsset: External octave-fuzz pedal (Univox Super-Fuzz or Fulltone Ultimate Octave clone) run into the GP-180's front input, bypassing the DST block's Fuzz model
proposals.reason: The GP-180 catalog has no dedicated octave-fuzz voicing, which is the most-cited distinguishing detail for this specific track in gear-forum discussion.
proposals.whenToUse: If the stock Fuzz model doesn't deliver enough upper-octave grit after testing.
proposals.expectedGain: More accurate vintage octave-fuzz bite on the main riff.

proposals.reason: Tuning (C F Bb Eb G C) and the octave-fuzz detail both rely on secondary/crowd-sourced material rather than a direct artist interview about this song; a rig-rundown or interview specifically covering 'Era Vulgaris' tracking would upgrade these from medium/low to high confidence.
proposals.whenToUse: Before treating tuning or fuzz-pedal specifics as authoritative in downstream use.
proposals.expectedGain: Higher-confidence sheet with fewer inferred details.
